questions.prompt: You need Azure Backup historical reports across several vaults. Which data path is documented for the reporting workbooks?

options.text: Vault diagnostic reporting logs sent to Log Analytics workspaces.
options.explanation: Reporting workbooks query exported backup diagnostic records in Azure Monitor Logs.

options.text: VM guest Heartbeat records sent to Log Analytics workspaces.
options.explanation: Guest heartbeats do not supply the backup job, policy and usage records required by these reports.

options.text: Vault metric charts without diagnostic-log export.
options.explanation: Metric charts do not provide the documented diagnostic-log data path for Backup Reports workbooks.

options.text: Recovery-point disk files copied directly into a workbook.
options.explanation: Workbooks query reporting records rather than storing or parsing restored VM disk files.

questions.prompt: Vault reporting diagnostics were enabled an hour ago. Today’s backup job is Completed, but Backup Reports has no row for it yet. Which interpretation should guide the next reporting check?

options.text: Recovery-point retention determines whether today’s row appears, so extend backup retention first.
options.explanation: Backup retention does not determine diagnostic delivery timing or completed-day report visibility.

options.text: A Completed backup job guarantees its report row is immediately available.
options.explanation: Operation completion is separate from diagnostic delivery and the reports’ completed-day convention.

options.text: Allow for initial diagnostic delivery, the current partial-day exclusion, and workspace/vault/time filters.
options.explanation: Initial delivery can take up to 24 hours, current partial-day data is omitted, and filters can further exclude records.

options.text: The report’s time picker can force partial-day rows to appear immediately.
options.explanation: Selecting today does not override the documented exclusion of current partial-day data.

questions.prompt: Backup recovery points are kept for a year, but the relevant Log Analytics reporting tables retain queryable data for 30 days. From now on, you need reporting over 90 completed days. Which change addresses the retention gap? Assume existing expired records cannot be recovered.

options.text: Extend only backup recovery-point retention to 90 days.
options.explanation: Recovery-point retention does not preserve the separate diagnostic records used for reports.

options.text: Extend the relevant queryable Log Analytics reporting-data retention to cover 90 days.
options.explanation: Reports require the underlying log records to remain queryable across the required period; retention and associated cost need review.

options.text: Change only the workbook’s time range to Last 90 days.
options.explanation: A wider query range cannot recover records that the reporting tables no longer retain.

options.text: Increase only the vault’s soft-delete retention to 90 days.
options.explanation: Soft-delete retention protects deleted backup data, not the queryable lifetime of reporting logs.
